newsitem.title: UK: Copper above $2,500, LME trade otherwise slow.
newsitem.headline: Copper above $2,500, LME trade otherwise slow.

text.p: Copper prices pushed higher during Tuesday LME pre-market trading, but the pace of trading was slow and there was little significant activity in the complex.
Three months prices flipped up from just under $2,500 to trade at $2,508 a tonne, a $20 gain from Monday's kerb close.
Traders said the market was well and truly in the summer doldrums - typified by Monday's low volumes and narrow trading ranges.
The warehouse stock report was generally supportive, with all metals recording lower inventory levels and with reasonably sized stock falls seen in copper and aluminium.
Copper stocks were down by 2,750 tonnes, which followed a 1,750-tonne drop on Monday, and compared with the smaller daily declines seen last week.
"The stock figures were a bit more encouraging, although it may not pay to read too much into them as about half was metal going back into Comex," one trader said.
If the market can sustain levels above $2,500, then there should be some technical follow-through.
Aluminium was trading $7 higher at $1,610 after a 2,875-tonne stock drawdown, although the market was again encountering resistance around those levels.
Tin prices jumped to $5,620, up $40 from yesterday, against the background of a 115-tonne inventory drawdown.
Lead and zinc were subdued and indicated at steady levels of $640/642 and $1,360/61 respectively. Alloy was quoted at $1,470/80.
